description: Comment mention: the third Agent launch trigger. Adding an issue comment emits com.mohist.issue.comment-added, and a system handler launches each @<agent> mentioned via the shared launcher (workspace-optional, comment-anchored idempotency).

tasks.title: Comment-added event: AddCommentAsync emits a lineage-stamped CloudEvent
tasks.description: Make the issue comment lifecycle a first-class event source. Add EventCatalog.ReverseDns.IssueCommentAdded = "com.mohist.issue.comment-added" and a standalone payload record { commentId, author, body } (NOT a new IssueEvent union variant — comments are a side record, not an aggregate state transition). Inject IEventStore into IssueGrain and, inside AddCommentAsync's existing save transaction, append the CloudEvent via IEventStore.AppendAsync(db, envelope) using IssueLineage.BuildExtensions(_issue) for stamping (the EpicGrain direct-emit pattern); poke the dispatcher after commit. IssueEventSerializer and the IssueEvent union stay untouched. This is the foundation T-002 subscribes to; it delivers no mention behavior yet.
acceptanceCriteria: Adding a comment (via POST /comments or mo issue comment add) emits exactly one com.mohist.issue.comment-added whose data carries the comment's commentId, author (normalized), and body verbatim.
The comment row is durable within the same transaction as the event append; a handler reading the comment by commentId always finds it (persistence-before-observable ordering).
The event's extensions always include projectid and issue (the issue number); epic is present when the issue belongs to an epic and omitted entirely otherwise — identical to other issue.* events.
Creating or editing an issue (including a body/title edit whose text contains an @) does NOT emit comment-added; only comment add emits it.

Spec tests (high-integration, server fakes per design/testing.md — no real bus/DB) assert the event payload, lineage stamping, and comment-only source; unit tests cover the IssueCommentAdded serialization + lineage build.
npm test (server) passes; C# build is warning-clean (TreatWarningsAsErrors).
tasks.output: EventCatalog.ReverseDns.IssueCommentAdded constant; IssueCommentAdded payload record; IEventStore injection into IssueGrain + emission in AddCommentAsync; spec + unit tests.
tasks.notes: See design D2 (direct CloudEvent, not an IssueEvent union variant — keeps the state-transition event family clean) and the Migration Plan step 1. Stamp with IssueLineage.BuildExtensions(_issue); reuse the EpicGrain EmitEvents pattern (IEventStore.AppendAsync(db, envelope) inside the tx + EventDispatcherPoke after commit).

tasks.title: Mention detection & launch: MentionDispatchHandler + comment-anchored launcher idempotency
tasks.description: Implement the comment-mention dispatch capability end-to-end. Add MentionDispatchHandler ([Subscription(Type = IssueCommentAdded)], ICloudEventHandler) that: loads the project's active Agents once; if the comment author matches an active Agent name (case-insensitive) skips mention detection (loop prevention); else parses @<token> mentions (regex @ followed by [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+, case-insensitive, deduped by resolved Agent id), resolves each via AgentQuerier.GetByNameAsync (active only — unresolved names log and continue, nothing launches), and launches each resolved Agent once. Launch MUST use the manual-style path (workspace-optional) so a mention fires on a backlog/terminal issue too — do NOT reuse RoutedAgentLaunchContextResolver/LaunchRoutedAsync, which require a nonterminal run+workspace and would preflight-fail exactly the backlog case the feature exists to serve. Extend AgentSessionResolver with a comment-anchored stable key hashing projectId\ncommentId\nagentId and extend IAgentLauncher (a thin mention launch entry or an explicit-anchor parameter on LaunchAsync) so the session id + AgentJob key are stable per (comment, agent) and trigger labels record mohist.io/trigger/event-id = comment event id + a new mohist.io/trigger/comment-id = comment id for bidirectional provenance. Prompt is the full comment body verbatim; context is the issue. The launcher extension + handler are one feature module (the handler is the only caller of the extension) — do not split them.
acceptanceCriteria: A human comment whose body @-mentions an active Agent launches that Agent once, with the full comment body (token unstripped) as prompt and the issue as context; it launches on a backlog issue (no workflow run) without any preflight failure — proving the workspace-optional manual-path decision.

Token parsing is whitespace/punctuation-delimited and case-insensitive (@SuperVisor resolves an Agent named supervisor); the same Agent @-mentioned repeatedly in one comment launches once; distinct @-mentions each launch independently; dedupe is by resolved Agent id.
A comment whose author matches an active Agent name (case-insensitive) is never scanned — no launch, no chain (loop prevention). A human-authored comment triggers normally.
@-ing a name with no active Agent match (including a name that matches only an archived Agent) launches nothing and records a structured log; the comment itself is unaffected.

Reprocessing the same comment (redelivered comment-added event) launches each resolved Agent at most once and creates no duplicate AgentJob — idempotency anchored on (projectId, commentId, agentId), not the event GUID. Two different comments mentioning the same Agent produce two launches (distinct commentId).
A mention produces exactly one AgentJob and creates no WatchEntry, routing subscription, or other persistent declaration.
The launched AgentJob's trigger labels carry the comment-added event id and the comment id, distinguishing a mention launch from routing/watch launches.

Spec tests (high-integration, injected fakes — no real network/grain/runner per design/testing.md) seed an Agent + comment and assert the full comment->launch behavior: backlog-issue launch, parsing/case/dedup, loop prevention, resolution-failure no-op, redelivery dedup, one-shot, and provenance labels. Unit tests cover the token parser and the comment-anchored stable-key derivation.
npm test (server) passes; C# build is warning-clean.
tasks.output: MentionDispatchHandler (subscription + parsing + loop prevention + resolution + launch); AgentSessionResolver comment-anchored stable-key entry; IAgentLauncher mention launch path + mohist.io/trigger/comment-id metadata constant; spec + unit tests.
tasks.notes: See design D1 (manual-style LaunchAsync, NOT LaunchRoutedAsync — the routed path's run+workspace requirement breaks the backlog headline use case; this reconciles the wording in design/agent-mentions.md), D3 (comment-anchored idempotency via AgentSessionResolver.StableId), D4 (regex token parser, name-only), D5 (declaration-based loop prevention), D6 (event-id + comment-id trigger labels). Open Question — mute interaction: implement the recommended default (an explicit @ overrides mute; MentionDispatchHandler does NOT consult WatchEntryStore). If the human decides mute should suppress mentions, add a WatchEntryStore muted-check in the handler before launching. Typo feedback (system reply/inbox) is out of scope — structured log only.
